progression.startsWith: Four bottles, A to D, each hold one unknown organic liquid. Your job isn't to name them. It's to say which functional groups your results support, and which ones they can't rule out. That takes three tests, the right controls beside each one, and a safe plan for the one reagent that contains chromium six.
progression.stopsAfter: stating the aim and the candidate classes; planning three tests on fresh portions; naming the variables; choosing a blank and a known for each test and explaining what each shows; describing the fizz test with its CO₂ check and the dichromate demonstration with its quantities; recording observations before inferences; stating supported, not detected and can't-tell claims for each unknown; judging validity, reliability and accuracy; writing the risk rows and the waste routes.

teaching.task: Four bottles, A to D, each hold one unknown organic liquid. How do you plan and run three quick tests, with the right controls and safely around chromium(VI), so that each claim you make about a functional group would stand up?
teaching.causalExplanation: (1) the job is supported claims, not names (1); (2) the aim, the candidate classes, the plan on fresh portions, who runs which test, and the variables (2); (3) the blank shows whether anything besides the sample caused a change; the known shows the reagent works and what a positive looks like (3); (4) bromine water by p02's method (4); (5) the carbonate test and its CO₂ check, read against the known and blank (5); (6) the dichromate demonstration: small volumes, water bath, no flame; batch 1 (6); (7) batch 2 with a repeat; green supports a 1° or 2° alcohol because there are no aldehyde candidates; orange means not detected (7); (8) record observation before inference, write in "no visible change", record the controls (8); (9) supported, not detected, can't tell; D (9); (10) validity, reliability, accuracy (10); (11) hazards, controls and waste (11); memory aid (12); attempts (13 to 16); decision rule and handoff (17); key notes (18).
teaching.conversationalApproach: Four bottles, A to D, each hold one unknown organic liquid. The aim: to test unknown organic liquids for a carbon to carbon double bond, a hydroxyl group and a carboxylic acid group. Every test needs two controls beside the unknown. You've already run the bromine water test, so use the same method, shown on the card. Put two millilitres of the unknown in a test tube. Now the dichromate test. The teacher runs A the same way, with repeats of A and D, and they stay orange. Record as you go, in a table drawn up beforehand. A fizzed, and its gas turned limewater milky, so a carboxylic acid is supported. Now the three words from the skills video. Now the risks. One line for your claims: supported, not detected, can't tell. Your turn. Not valid. Last one. The fizz and the milky limewater support a carboxylic acid. So, for any unknown organic liquid: three tests on fresh portions, a blank and a known beside each, observations before inferences, and only the claims your results support.
teaching.openingDecision: Four bottles, A to D, each hold one unknown organic liquid. Your job isn't to name them. It's to say which functional groups your results support, and which ones they can't rule out. That takes three tests, the right controls beside each one, and a safe plan for the one reagent that contains chromium six.
teaching.understandingCheck: Two, each 10 s with the countdown and every condition visible: A1's rinse, the four contents including the water blank, the bath, "all four turned green" and the conclusion; A2's candidate classes, three observations, the limewater result and the blanks. Nothing answer-bearing during the holds.
teaching.curriculumScope:
Syllabus dotpoint (as printed; NSW Chemistry Stage 6, 2017, p58; C8-IQ2-01 is this project's local catalogue ID, not a code printed in the syllabus), quoted from ../../programme/syllabus/chem-2017-y12.json:

"conduct qualitative investigations to test for the presence in organic molecules of the following functional groups:
- carbon–carbon double bonds
- hydroxyl groups
- carboxylic acids (ACSCH130)"

(The dash in "carbon–carbon" is an en dash as printed, not an em dash.) The tests and their reasoning were chem-m8-c08. This video is the investigation: planning it, choosing controls, running it safely, recording it and stating supported claims.

design.visualSystem: no people, hands or faces (drops, the spatula, shaking, the bung and the dropper are coded motion); apparatus as painted plates listed by filename, never stretched, never cross-faded between different rack sets; at most about three bright text items, earlier lines dim; one reasoning stage at a time; "Pause here to answer." then a 10 s countdown with the full worded question kept on screen; no givens card in the attempts, givens underlined in the feedback as they are used; brief feedback (answer, key reason, one crossed mistake, about 15 to 30 s); original HSC-style questions only; real GHS classifications, schools' own risk assessments named in the footer; Australian spelling; no em dashes; conversational narration; no absolute claims ("supports", "not detected", "usually"); optional key notes hold.
design.transitionPlan: heading writes on: "Unknown organics: which claims can you back?". task line "Aim: test unknowns for C=C, –OH, –COOH". the board clears. task line "Test 2: bromine water (p02 method)". task line "Test 1: NaHCO₃ fizz". task line "Test 3: acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ (teacher demonstration)". the after plate slides left and shrinks. the board clears. the claims card fills in the right third, one row per unknown as spoken: "A | supported: –COOH | not detected: C=C, 1° or 2° –OH"; "C | supported: C=C | not detected: –COOH | can't tell: –OH (no dichromate test)"; "B | supported: 1° or 2° –OH | not detected: C=C, –COOH"; "D | supported: none | not detected: C=C, –COOH, 1° or 2° –OH | can't tell: alkane or 3° alcohol". task line "Valid? Reliable? Accurate?". during the speech only the current row of the risk table is on screen, large, as a single "Hazard / Harm / Control" line: chromium(VI) (on "waste"), flammable organics (on "flame"), bromine water (on "Bromine vapour"), smelling (on "Never smell": hazard "vapours of unknowns", control "observe colour and bubbles only"), waste (on "sink"). the board clears. the board clears. the card stays, shrunk to the top. question card, worded as printed (A2 under Decisions), set as a short results list with the blanks in grey brackets. the card stays, shrunk to the top. the board clears. Heading on screen: "Key notes: what to write in your book".
